speakers.name: Innocent Mbuvi
speakers.biography_html:
Innocent Mbuvi is an Odoo Functional Consultant at Odoo, turning SME implementations into systems teams actually use  not just admire in a demo. He works with businesses still running on spreadsheets and memory, bringing the structure that makes running things easier: streamlining messy manual processes, and designing websites  from online stores to brand sites  that give those businesses a face online as sharp as the operations behind them.

He's driven by a simple belief African SMEs deserve tooling built to the same standard as global enterprises, not a scaled-down version of it. At OXP26, he brings that lens to the Website Builder: a corner of Odoo most people scroll past, and one with more to offer than it gets credit for.

speakers.name: Vivian Anyona
speakers.biography_html:
Vivian Anyona is a Business Analyst and Payroll Localization Specialist with experience in designing and implementing payroll solutions for African markets. She has played a key role in developing and localizing Odoo Payroll for Kenya, supporting a solution that has impacted more than 10,000 users over three years.

Her work combines payroll compliance, HR processes, business analysis, and Odoo configuration, translating complex statutory requirements into practical and scalable payroll solutions. She has also been involved in payroll localization initiatives across Kenya, South Africa, and Zambia, with a focus on understanding local legislation, designing payroll rules, and documenting solutions for broader adoption.

Vivian is passionate about demonstrating that Africa’s diverse payroll requirements are not a barrier to digital transformation and that with the right expertise, payroll can be engineered to meet local needs.

He brings focused expertise in Inventory and Manufacturing, helping businesses streamline supply chains, strengthen warehouse operations, and build production processes that scale.

Kevin works closely with manufacturers and distributors to design solutions that reflect local realities while enabling international-grade efficiency, helping clients cut costs, eliminate bottlenecks, and grow sustainably.

As an Odoo specialist, Kevin Wamae is a trusted partner for African businesses seeking to modernize operations and build lasting competitive advantage.

speakers.name: Elijah Ssebugwawo
speakers.biography_html:
Elijah Ssebugwawo is the Managing Director and Founder of a Kampala-based corporate group encompassing Gadget Craze, Gridlink Cargo Solutions, and Gateway Core Sourcing.

Driven by an obsession with consumer electronics and a refusal to accept the fragmented retail experiences available at the time, Elijah launched Gadget Craze in 2012 at just 20 years old. What began as a singular vision to bring premium tech to East Africa has since evolved into a dynamic e-commerce and logistics ecosystem.

A hands-on technologist with a relentless drive for operational efficiency, Elijah recognized early on that scaling a high-demand business required more than just front-end sales—it demanded a bulletproof backend. This systems-first mindset led him to champion the adoption of Odoo, successfully architecting the company's transition from a constrained, single-storefront startup into a streamlined, multi-entity powerhouse.

When he isn’t optimizing ERP architecture, managing staging databases, or executing corporate strategy, Elijah is an avid gamer and automotive enthusiast who remains deeply passionate about pushing the boundaries of the East African tech landscape.

speakers.name: Ajeet Kumar Yadav
speakers.biography_html:
Ajeet Kumar Yadav is the visionary CEO of Softprime Consulting Pvt Ltd, a leading digital transformation firm specializing in Odoo ERP solutions. With over a decade of hands-on experience in ERP implementation, Python development, and business process automation, Ajeet has established himself as a certified Odoo expert and a trusted advisor to enterprises across the world.​

Under his leadership, Softprime has grown into a multi-regional powerhouse, delivering over 400 successful Odoo projects across sectors such as energy, healthcare, manufacturing, and logistics. Ajeet's strategic focus on AI-driven automation, IoT integration, and scalable ERP architecture has positioned the company as a go-to partner for complex, multi-company deployments.​

Ajeet is particularly recognized for leading the digital transformation of Horn Petroleum Group, where he oversaw the implementation of a centralized Odoo-based ERP system supporting over 100 users across multiple business units. This initiative streamlined operations, enhanced real-time visibility, and introduced predictive analytics, setting a new benchmark for ERP success in the energy sector.​

Beyond his technical acumen, Ajeet is a passionate advocate for open-source innovation and sustainable digital growth. He continues to mentor emerging tech leaders and actively contributes to the Odoo community.

speakers.function: Founder/CEO of Kytabu Africa and Tribbe Nation
speakers.biography_html:
Tonee Ndungu is a Kenyan entrepreneur who has spent his career helping build what many now call Kenya’s Silicon Savannah. His belief in technology’s power to transform lives runs deep, and he has dedicated his work to unlocking Africa’s social and economic potential through innovation and access.

His entrepreneurial journey is one of faith over form. Born dyslexic, he founded the NAILAB in 2009, started KYTABU in 2012 to make education more accessible, and is now building Tribbe — a fintech platform designed to digitize social finance and community credit, redefining Africa’s social capital.

He is committed to advancing Africa’s voice in the global AI conversation. His work focuses on educating and inspiring a generation of African entrepreneurs who see AI not as a threat, but as a tool to create opportunity from adversity.

“Whatever you do, don’t leave this world without building something for others.”

Born dyslexic, he founded the NAILAB in 2009, started KYTABU in 2012 to make education more accessible, and is now building Tribbe — a fintech platform designed to digitize social finance and community credit, redefining Africa’s social capital.
He is committed to advancing Africa’s voice in the global AI conversation. His work focuses on educating and inspiring a generation of African entrepreneurs who see AI not as a threat, but as a tool to create opportunity from adversity.
“Whatever you do, don’t leave this world without building something for others.”

He brings extensive regional experience across East Africa and the Indian Ocean. As Visa International's Lead for Merchant Acceptance in the region for six years, he played a pivotal role in expanding payment acceptance in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Mauritius, Seychelles, and Madagascar.

Payroll is logic and logic can be engineered.

Key learnings for the audience:
• Designing conversational interfaces for HR workflows
• Building WhatsApp integrations with Odoo HRM
• Asynchronous approval workflows and notification patterns
• User adoption strategies for mobile-first HR tools
• Backend architecture for real-time leave balance queries

Value for attendees: HR technology leaders and Odoo developers will learn how to bridge the gap between modern employee expectations and legacy HR systems. The session demonstrates that powerful HR automation doesn't require complex portals — it requires meeting employees where they are.

Target audience: Odoo developers, HR technology specialists, companies with distributed workforces, and organizations seeking to improve employee experience with modern communication tools.

tracks.description_html:
Scaling a high-demand consumer electronics and logistics business in East Africa requires a robust backend, but our early operations were holding us back. Initially relying on a fragmented tech stack built around WordPress, we faced significant growing pains: we couldn't accurately manage our inventory, manual invoicing was tedious, and tracking our financial records was a constant challenge. Furthermore, our sales team relied on ordinary mobile phones and native WhatsApp, leading to siloed, unorganized communication with our clients.

In this Customer Success Story, discover how migrating to Odoo solved these critical pain points and became the central nervous system for our business. We will explore how Odoo provided the technical foundation needed to transition from a struggling single storefront into a streamlined, three-entity corporate group—encompassing Gadget Craze, Gridlink Cargo Solutions, and Gateway Core Sourcing.

We will showcase how replacing our disconnected tools with Odoo's unified ecosystem allowed us to bridge CRM, complex multi-company inventory, and accounting. Additionally, we will highlight how upgrading from native mobile WhatsApp to a fully integrated WhatsApp solution within Odoo transformed our customer engagement, bringing all client communication into one centralized, traceable hub.


Key takeaways for attendees will include:

  • Overcoming the E-commerce Bottleneck: Escaping the limitations of a basic WordPress setup to achieve real-time, accurate inventory and financial tracking.
  • Centralizing Client Communication: Transitioning from scattered mobile phone WhatsApp chats to a streamlined, omnichannel customer engagement strategy using Odoo CRM and WhatsApp integration.
  • Mastering the Multi-Company Environment: Leveraging Odoo to smoothly manage distinct corporate entities (retail, logistics, and trading) without data silos or operational downtime.
  • Technical Stability: Practical insights into utilizing Odoo.sh and staging databases to maintain system stability and execute safe updates.
tracks.description_text:
Scaling a high-demand consumer electronics and logistics business in East Africa requires a robust backend, but our early operations were holding us back. Initially relying on a fragmented tech stack built around WordPress, we faced significant growing pains: we couldn't accurately manage our inventory, manual invoicing was tedious, and tracking our financial records was a constant challenge. Furthermore, our sales team relied on ordinary mobile phones and native WhatsApp, leading to siloed, unorganized communication with our clients.
In this Customer Success Story, discover how migrating to Odoo solved these critical pain points and became the central nervous system for our business. We will explore how Odoo provided the technical foundation needed to transition from a struggling single storefront into a streamlined, three-entity corporate group—encompassing Gadget Craze, Gridlink Cargo Solutions, and Gateway Core Sourcing.
We will showcase how replacing our disconnected tools with Odoo's unified ecosystem allowed us to bridge CRM, complex multi-company inventory, and accounting. Additionally, we will highlight how upgrading from native mobile WhatsApp to a fully integrated WhatsApp solution within Odoo transformed our customer engagement, bringing all client communication into one centralized, traceable hub.
Key takeaways for attendees will include:
Overcoming the E-commerce Bottleneck: Escaping the limitations of a basic WordPress setup to achieve real-time, accurate inventory and financial tracking.
Centralizing Client Communication: Transitioning from scattered mobile phone WhatsApp chats to a streamlined, omnichannel customer engagement strategy using Odoo CRM and WhatsApp integration.
Mastering the Multi-Company Environment: Leveraging Odoo to smoothly manage distinct corporate entities (retail, logistics, and trading) without data silos or operational downtime.
Technical Stability: Practical insights into utilizing Odoo.sh and staging databases to maintain system stability and execute safe updates.

This systems-first mindset led him to champion the adoption of Odoo, successfully architecting the company's transition from a constrained, single-storefront startup into a streamlined, multi-entity powerhouse.

When he isn’t optimizing ERP architecture, managing staging databases, or executing corporate strategy, Elijah is an avid gamer and automotive enthusiast who remains deeply passionate about pushing the boundaries of the East African tech landscape.

The session will show how agriculture workflows can be combined with Odoo’s ERP capabilities to create a practical solution for African agribusinesses. From farm records to stock movement, from production planning to sales, and from operational activities to financial reports, Agric Things helps bring visibility, accountability, and control into agriculture operations.

Attendees will learn how Odoo can be used not only as an ERP, but as a strong foundation for building agriculture platforms that support real farm operations, value chain management, and scalable agribusiness growth.

tracks.name: Smart Payments: ERP-Driven Banking with Built-In Fraud Detection and Decision Assurance
tracks.speaker_line: Hari Bhogaita
tracks.description_html:
This talk presents a real-world, production-grade ERP-bank integration that delivers real-time control, automated reconciliation, and built-in fraud prevention across all financial transactions. Payments are executed directly from the ERP, incoming funds are receipted instantly, and reconciliation can be completed automatically, eliminating manual intervention, reducing errors, and removing the risk of fictitious or manipulated transactions.

Unlike traditional approaches that rely on external banking platforms or third-party wallet systems, this is a direct integration with banks. There is no wallet involved, no need to preload funds, and no intermediary layer. All transactions are executed directly from and into the organisation’s actual bank accounts, ensuring full alignment with existing banking structures, controls, and compliance requirements.

The system is already fully implemented and operational, supporting a wide range of payment types including KRA iTax, RTGS, PesaLink, SWIFT, mobile money (M-Pesa), and standard bank transfers. It is currently integrated with major institutions such as I&M Bank, M-Pesa, and Equity Bank, with additional banks being onboarded, enabling organisations to operate across multiple payment rails from a single unified ERP platform.

Beyond outbound payments, the system also handles inbound transactions through instant payment notifications. When money is received into a bank account, the ERP is notified in real time and can automatically generate a payment receipt without any manual input. For example, if a supplier’s bank account details change after a history of payments to a different account, the system will automatically flag the transaction for additional scrutiny. It also performs cross-checks such as identifying when a supplier is also a customer with outstanding balances, prompting users to consider netting off payments instead of making unnecessary disbursements.

Looking ahead, this protocol is being extended into AI-driven capabilities that will analyse transaction patterns, detect anomalies, and proactively flag potential fraud risks before payments are executed.

It also demonstrates how organisations can move away from fragmented banking interfaces and adopt a single, ERP-driven financial control layer.

tracks.description_html:

Brief Description

Accounting is one of the most important areas in any Odoo implementation because it is where business owners, finance teams, auditors, and management expect accuracy, control, and reliable reporting. In many African businesses, finance teams are still dealing with manual Excel reconciliations, unclear chart of accounts, weak closing controls, delayed bank reconciliations, tax compliance pressure, disconnected sales and inventory processes, and historical data challenges.

This talk will share practical lessons on how to implement and use Odoo Accounting effectively in real business environments. The session will focus on key setup decisions such as chart of accounts, taxes, journals, fiscal periods, document sequences, user access rights, lock dates, opening balances, customer and vendor balances, and bank accounts. It will also show how Accounting connects with Sales, Purchase, Inventory, POS, Manufacturing, Projects, Payroll, Expenses, and local compliance processes such as tax reporting and eTIMS/KRA requirements.

Attendees will learn how to avoid common accounting implementation mistakes, improve bank reconciliation, strengthen month-end closing, improve audit readiness, and build reports that management can trust. The session is ideal for business owners, accountants, finance managers, Odoo consultants, implementation partners, and organizations planning to use Odoo Accounting as the financial control center of their business.

tracks.name: What's New in Payroll?
tracks.speaker_line: Alan Keith Lavuna, Business Analyst at Odoo
tracks.description_html:
Smarter Configuration, Simpler Workflows

From dynamic salary packages to a redesigned Payrun workflow — see how Odoo Payroll is evolving to reduce manual work, prevent errors, and give employees more control over their own benefits.

Payroll is getting smarter and more configurable. This session covers two major threads: how salary packages and employee benefits are now configured, and the deeper workflow redesign coming with Odoo 20.

We'll start with salary package configuration — walking through how rules are set up and how they flow through to the employee's Payroll tab in real time. From there, we'll show how the newly evolved Attendances app, with its advanced overtime tracking methods, now directly affects Time Off and Payroll calculations, setting up a natural bridge into the Attendance session.

Key Highlights:

Salary Packages & Employee Benefits

  • Dynamic allowance calculations, accurate medical insurance cost adjustments, and PF opt-in/out support for precise salary and contribution computations
  • Applicants can now select their preferred time-off benefits directly during the offer signing process
  • Streamlined setup and management of statutory compliance reports — PF, PT, LWF, ESIC, and Gratuity Calculation

Efficient Payroll Management with Odoo 20

  • Work Entries have been retired — Work Entry Types are now consolidated with Time Off Types
  • Reworked Working Schedules let you define daily working hours without fixed start/end times
  • A redesigned Payrun workflow guides users through every processing step, with employee inclusion now automatically managed from attendance and time-off records
  • Salary simulation is now available directly from the employee profile, prefilled with relevant data
  • New configurable payslip delivery settings — send on confirmation, on payment, or manually
  • Support for arrears compensation, covering underpayments from prior periods due to errors, delays, or backdated salary changes

Turn Alerts into Actions — Right from Your Payroll Dashboard

  • A redesigned Payroll Dashboard with smart warnings, helping users catch setup issues early and manage day-to-day payroll activity more efficiently

tracks.name: Business First: Choosing the Right Odoo Platform
tracks.speaker_line: Enock Maseru, Business Analyst at Odoo
tracks.description_html:
Choosing the right Odoo platform is more than a technical decision — it’s a business decision that can shape how easily your company grows, adapts, and manages costs over the long term. Deciding between Odoo Online, Odoo.sh, and On-Premise is one of the most important decisions in any Odoo implementation. Each platform offers different trade-offs in terms of customization, maintenance, cost, scalability, and technical requirements.

Drawing from real implementation experiences, this session provides a practical framework for selecting the right platform based on business requirements and long-term goals. We'll discuss when Odoo Online is the best fit, when Odoo.sh becomes necessary for custom developments and complex workflows, and why On-Premise should generally be reserved for organizations with strong technical capacity or strict data governance requirements.

We'll also share practical implementation insights, including why starting on Odoo Online and planning a future migration to Odoo.sh can often be the most effective approach. The goal is simple: choose the platform that fits where your business is today and where you want it to go — not the one that simply appeals to your technical team.

Outline

  • Understanding Odoo Online, Odoo.sh, and On-Premise
  • When standard Odoo is enough—and when it isn't
  • The hidden costs of customization and self-hosting
  • Real implementation lessons learned from business analysts
  • A practical decision framework for partners and implementers

Key Takeaways

  • Select the right platform based on business needs, not technical preferences
  • Understand the risks and benefits of each deployment model
  • Learn when to customize, when to stay standard, and when to migrate
  • Apply proven implementation practices to reduce project risk and complexity

tracks.name: Outgrower Management System (OMS): Digitising Smallholder Value Chains
tracks.speaker_line: Dennis, Consultant
tracks.description_html:
African agribusiness runs on thousands of smallholder farmers, often registered and transacted with in the field, frequently offline. This session presents our Outgrower Management System (OMS) – an Odoo-based product that brings farmer registration, contracting, training, offtake and input supply into one connected platform.
Field-first with Kobo Toolbox
OMS pairs Odoo with Kobo Toolbox, so field teams capture data on mobile – even offline – and submissions create the right records back in Odoo. Each survey is packaged as a reusable product, with master data (regions, communities, districts, seasons, products, farmer groups, farmers) fed from Odoo to Kobo so field choices stay consistent.
• Farmer registration & contracts. Register farmers and groups, capture details (name, phone, MoMo, ID, gender, acreage, group role), create the farmer as verified, and generate season/crop/acreage contracts in draft for confirmation in Odoo.
• Training attendance & interactions. Log training sessions and participants by farmer group, and record field interactions against each farmer.
• Offtake & input orders. Crop buying creates a confirmed purchase order, goods receipt and posted bill with payment registration; input sales create a confirmed sales order, delivery and posted invoice – all from a single field submission.
The standout: Payment in Kind
OMS lets input orders given to farmers on “loan” be offset against the crop they later sell. A dedicated repayment-in-kind journal tracks outstanding farmer balances; at offtake payment, the purchase can be deducted against the outstanding loan, with optional reconciliation so finance can choose to offset or pay the farmer. Balances are tracked right through to the aged-receivable report.

tracks.name: How a Gold Partner Scales Implementation & Support
tracks.speaker_line: Ivo, Project Director
tracks.description_html:
Great functional work fails if delivery falls apart. This session shares the Advance Insight method – our Implementation Bible and Project Management & Support manual – that has let us move from small projects to six-figure programmes while keeping projects under control and customers satisfied after go-live.
The core principle
“Implement one MVP at a time.” The client signs off each element in a UAT tracking sheet before we move on. The focus is on the flow first; access rights, approvals and master data are tightened later. As we put it internally: don’t fix the plane while you’re in mid-air – and it’s better to not be billable than to waste budget.
What we cover
• Roles & structure. A clear split between the client SPOC and our Lead Consultant, with Project Director and management as the escalation path, and a train-the-trainer approach.
• Cadence & reporting. Daily channel, weekly alignment call and bi-weekly/monthly management report; weekly progress, decisions log and timesheet reporting on hourly elements, with budget overruns flagged early.
• Prioritisation. A simple decision tree – master data and bugs first, engineering tasks and user mistakes next, change requests and scoping last – with response targets for each.
• Environment discipline on Odoo.sh. Main / Client-QA / Internal-QA structure, rebuilds from Main, controlled code merges, and a deliberate “avoid Studio, raise engineering tickets” stance.
• Change & escalation. A formal change-request procedure with written approval, and an escalation model that loops in the Project Director before issues boil over.
• Support that scales. Support typed as bugs, user mistakes, training or change requests; bug severity SLAs (Sev 1 in ~4 business hours, Sev 2 in 1 day, Sev 3 best-effort); a 3-month warranty; and bi-annual database health checks tied to client check-ins.

We’ll look at the key new features, practical use cases, and improvements to the Planning experience, with a focus on how businesses can use these updates to simplify scheduling, improve team visibility, and optimize resource allocation.
